security_audit.summary: Static external-command alerts are Markdown backticks and template text; no shell execution or network exfiltration was found. Two local filesystem hardening issues remain: unvalidated skill names can escape the requested output root, and packaging zips every file under a skill folder. Harden these paths before automated use with untrusted inputs.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated skill names can control output paths.
remediation.suggestion: Reject absolute paths, path separators, traversal segments, and names outside a strict hyphen-case pattern. Resolve the final path and ensure it stays under the output root.

remediation.issue: Package archives include every file in the skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Add exclusions for .env, .git, caches, temporary files, generated archives, and common secret files. Print the included file list before writing the zip.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Skill Name Allows Out-of-Root Writes
semantic_findings.description: scripts/init_skill.py uses the provided skill name directly when building the output path. Absolute paths or path traversal segments can create the generated skill outside the requested output directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script reads skill_name from argv and joins it into a filesystem path without enforcing its printed hyphen-case requirement. It then creates directories and files at that computed path.

semantic_findings.title: Packaging Recursively Includes All Skill Files
semantic_findings.description: scripts/package_skill.py adds every file under the selected skill directory to the release archive. Secrets, temporary files, or generated archives can be included if they are present in that folder.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code walks skill_path.rglob("*") and writes every file it sees. This is common packaging behavior, but it lacks an exclusion list or final inclusion confirmation.

content.value_statement: Creating reusable AI skills can be inconsistent when structure, triggers, and resources are unclear. This skill provides a repeatable workflow for planning, initializing, validating, and packaging skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to structure SKILL.md frontmatter and usage instructions.
Guides planning from concrete user examples to reusable resources.
Initializes a template skill directory with example scripts, references, and assets.
Validates required frontmatter and naming conventions before packaging.
Packages a validated skill folder into a distributable zip archive.
Recommends when to use scripts, references, and assets.
limitations: Generated template content still requires manual editing before release.
Validation is basic and does not perform deep security review.
Scripts write files locally and require careful path selection.
Packaging can include unwanted files unless the folder is clean.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Skill
use_cases.description: Turn concrete user examples into a focused skill outline with resources and workflow steps.

use_cases.title: Build a Skill Package
use_cases.description: Create a starter skill folder, validate metadata, and prepare a distributable archive.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Guidance
use_cases.description: Convert repeated internal workflows into reusable AI instructions with references, scripts, and assets.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new skill for [task]. Ask up to three questions, then propose the SKILL.md sections and bundled resources.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize a Starter Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skill creator workflow to initialize a skill named [skill-name] under [path], then list the files to edit.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this existing skill for trigger clarity, progressive disclosure, reusable resources, and validation gaps. Suggest targeted edits.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare for Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these usage examples and resource needs into a complete skill structure, validation checklist, and packaging plan for release.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for cleaning PDF forms.
output_examples.output: A skill plan with trigger examples, needed PDF helper scripts, resource folders, and validation steps.
A review focused on trigger clarity, SKILL.md structure, reusable references, and unnecessary sample files.
A packaging checklist covering required metadata, folder cleanup, validation results, and archive contents.

best_practices: Start with concrete user examples before writing instructions.
Keep SKILL.md focused and move detailed reference material into reference files.
Validate and package only after placeholder content is removed.
anti_patterns: Leaving generated TODO sections in the final skill.
Putting large reference manuals directly into SKILL.md.
Packaging sample assets or scripts that the final skill does not use.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create reusable AI skills with structured instructions, supporting resources, validation, and packaging guidance.

faq.question: Does it write a complete final skill automatically?
faq.answer: It creates a starter structure and process. The user or agent must still replace placeholder content.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it package a skill for sharing?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a packager that validates the skill and creates a zip archive.

faq.question: Does it include security validation?
faq.answer: Only basic validation is included. Review scripts, packaged files, and user-controlled paths before publishing.

faq.question: When should I use references or assets?
faq.answer: Use references for detailed guidance. Use assets for templates, media, fonts, or boilerplate files used in outputs.
